title: Type an App: Convert a To-Do App to TypeScript
instructions: Submit exactly one file containing the complete TypeScript implementation of the TodoApp class with all type annotations and interface definitions. Include the Task interface and the fully typed class. Do not change the original logic. Do not submit a folder or ZIP.

rubrics.full: Defines a Task interface with correctly typed properties for id (number), title (string), completed (boolean), and createdAt (Date).
rubrics.partial: Defines a Task interface but has incorrect property types or missing properties.
rubrics.zero: Does not define a Task interface or the interface is incorrect.

rubrics.full: Adds correct type annotations to class properties (tasks array, nextId number) and uses the Task interface appropriately.
rubrics.partial: Adds some property types but misses annotations or uses incorrect types (e.g., any for the tasks array).
rubrics.zero: Does not add type annotations to class properties.

rubrics.full: Adds correct type annotations to all method parameters and return types, handling nullable returns appropriately.
rubrics.partial: Adds type annotations to most methods but misses some or has incorrect return types (e.g., not handling null returns).
rubrics.zero: Does not add type annotations to method parameters or return types.

rubrics.full: The implementation is fully type-safe without using any, preserves the original behavior, and correctly handles all operations.
rubrics.partial: The implementation is mostly type-safe but has unnecessary any usage or minor type issues, or has minor behavior differences.
rubrics.zero: The implementation relies on any, changes the original behavior, or does not compile.

valid_alternatives: Use a type alias instead of an interface for the Task type.
Use readonly for the id property if appropriate.
Use array methods that maintain type safety without explicit type assertions.
Add optional chaining or nullish coalescing if appropriate for error handling.
mistakes_to_check: Using any for the tasks array or task objects instead of the Task interface (type safety).
Not typing the return type of deleteTask as Task | null or similar (nullable returns).
Missing type annotations for method parameters like title and id (parameter types).
Changing the original logic or behavior while adding types (behavior preservation).
Not defining the Task interface with all required properties (interface completeness).
